## bijection_verdict

**PASS.**

Within the audited domain of this task — three baselines, thirteen factor ladders with every tier,
five base policies, four retired clauses, thirteen catalogue tables and three tool contracts — the
correspondence is lossless at the level of entailment: nothing unborne, nothing borne with changed
meaning, and no claim from outside the source. Both prerequisite sentences stand verbatim, in their
declared state form, in a document of the policy they block and in no other policy's, and both hops
are resolvable at the source's strength from that sentence, the depended-on documents and the
records.

Relation to previous revisions: this is revision 1; there is no earlier `policy_kb` file for this
difficulty.

### Policy-side notes (reported, not counted toward this skill's verdict)

- **P1 — "struck in whole bushels" has no rounding mode.** The phrase governs the result of all three
  computations in this task, and neither the source's `rule`/`baseline.rule` nor the KB says whether
  it rounds or truncates; only the `compute` expression `RND(…, 0)` pins it. In this task the
  restated commitment comes to 15,136.552 before the striking, so the reader must choose between
  15,136 and 15,137 — and the choice moves the buyout charge between 830.40 and 830.56. The documents
  are faithful to the source; the gap is the source's. (The undelivered bushels, 3,059.29, resolve to
  3,059 on either convention.)
- **P4 — an in-force clause whose defining sentence is retired.** `closing_out_bushels_already_sold`
  carries, as a clause in force, "Where the market has fallen the loss is zero and only the
  administrative fee is charged; the cooperative does not pay the member the difference" — the
  source's own in-force clause — while the sentence that defined the market loss is retired by
  `overwrite` and the extended buyout charge carries no market-loss term at all. A reader is left
  with a clause about a quantity nothing in force defines. The KB carries the source faithfully; the
  residue is the source's.
- **P6 — catalogue charges no write books.** The Minimum Price Contract's setup fee of 85.00
  "charged once, when the contract is countersigned", its amendment fee of 75.00 "charged whether or
  not the amendment later proves unnecessary" and its extension charge of 0.020 per bushel for moving
  the last day out are all normative in the catalogue, and none of the three task tools in this chain
  takes a parameter that books any of them. The documents carry the source faithfully; recorded so it
  is on the record.

## dependency_form

Basis: the blind answer's hop marks for this task (both hops **state-derived**, neither pre-solved)
and a full read of the 73-document corpus.

### Checks that came back clean

- **No state-form sentence restated as an action.** Both prerequisite sentences in this chain are
  `form: state`, each appears verbatim exactly once in the whole scenario, in a document of the
  problem it blocks, and neither hub restates it in action terms.
  `buying_out_an_undelivered_balance` never says "register the amendment first" or names the
  amendment as the thing that moves the window; it says only what the charge waits on.
  `registering_a_written_amendment` never says "countersign first"; it says only what the restated
  commitment waits on. The performer, the act and the route are what the reader works out from
  `registering_a_written_amendment`'s and `countersigning_a_grain_contract_application`'s own rules
  and from the contract record.
- **No other problem's tool name.** Each recorded act is named in exactly one document — its own
  hub's "How it is invoked" block. The blocked hubs name their own tool only.
- **No route, no aggregated chain, no ordered step list across problems.** No document carries a
  dependency table, a checklist, a roadmap or a procedure spanning two problems. The ordering
  sentences elsewhere in the corpus are base-law clauses the source itself states — "A signed master
  grain marketing agreement covering the crop year of the contract is on file for the member before
  the contract is opened"; "An amendment is signed and registered no later than the amendment window
  running from the day the contract was countersigned" — which the KB may neither drop nor soften;
  these are policy-side notes under Step 4, not KB findings.
- **No dependency stated in a second document.** Exact-string search over `docs/*/*.json` confirms
  each of the five prerequisite sentences appears in exactly one document, and the depended-on side
  never discloses who waits on it.
- **No contrast of a wrong with a correct reading, no named mistake, no cross-problem worked example
  or FAQ.** Every "Points of judgement" section stays inside one policy.
- **Titles and openings.** "Buying Out the Undelivered Balance of a Contract", "Registering a Written
  Amendment Against a Live Contract", "Countersigning an Application and Binding It for the Bushels
  Agreed", "The Bushels a Contract Is Countersigned For", "What a Buyout Comes To on a Grain
  Marketing Contract" — all general subjects. "What a Written Change Leaves a Contract Committing **on
  a Short Crop**" names the general subject the policy is defined by (its own baseline rule opens "A
  member whose crop has come in short of the bushels they sold is amended in writing rather than left
  to run into default"), so it is not a mirror of this task's situation. No opening restates a
  customer request.
- **Baselines silent about variation.** `bushels_a_contract_is_countersigned_for`
  ("No hauled-load credit is added. The forward reserve is the standard forward reserve of 3000
  bushels"), `what_a_written_change_leaves_the_contract_committing` ("The credited bushels are then
  reduced by the hold shrink, which is nil, and the retained share of the shortfall is the whole of
  it") and `what_a_buyout_comes_to` ("The patron release factor is one … No collection charge is
  added") each state their defaults flat, with no hedge, no exception list, no "unless otherwise
  provided" and no pointer.
- **No factor document says which tier a customer falls on**, describes a reading to avoid, or writes
  a task's evidence rows in as fact. Search for "this member", "the caller", "most members", "in this
  case", "mistake", "wrongly" returns nothing.
- **Findability without borrowed phrasing.** "the last day of the contract's delivery window", "the
  bushels the contract commits", "countersigned and binding on both sides" and "the committed bushels
  it was countersigned for" are the words the records and the prerequisite sentences use, and they
  are the words the depended-on documents use; neither hop needed phrasing borrowed from the
  dependent document.

### One observation, falling short of RED

`loss_multiplier_and_what_was_delivered_2c7424ef.json` — a factor document inside this task's scope —
uses, in its illustration, "9,000 undelivered bushels **at a release rate of 0.16**". 0.16 is the
*delivered release rate*, a tier value of the `release_rate_basis` factor carried in a different
document, and it matches no programme's default penalty, which is what the buyout baseline gives as
the release rate. A reader who cross-checks could infer from it that some other release rate exists.
I stop short of `KB-EXPLICIT RED` because the figure is framed as a hypothetical, states no condition
under which it applies, and the release-rate ladder is in any case discoverable from the contract's
programme; it is recorded so the judgement can be rechecked.

**PASS.**
